Neha / Karthik — reviewed the ask and the numbers. Recommendation below (balanced to preserve close):

1) Ramp schedule: approve a temporary ramp at 70% for month 1 and 85% for month 2 (applies to first 90 days of service), with a return-to-commit clause that normalizes usage expectations for billing months 4+. We avoid a 60% floor because that undermines committed minimums and complicates autoscale economics.

2) Early termination: counter-propose a capped early-exit credit of 25% of the remaining committed spend if termination occurs within the first 90 days; if termination occurs months 4–6, credit steps down to 15%. No credit after 6 months. Cap the total payment to the customer at $150k or remaining committed spend, whichever is lower. Rationale: protects us from immediate revenue loss while giving the customer flexibility.

3) Conditions: client must provide 30 days' written notice and allow Redwood to run a specified transition export (log export + KV snapshot) for auditing. Also require that any early-exit payment is net of outstanding invoices.

Next steps: Karthik — please provide any legal redlines to the above language. If legal signs off, I request Vivek provide exec sign-off on the capped credit for this account given its strategic fit.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts

Marissa / Neha — quick legal take after reviewing the draft:

1) Early termination credit: the stepped approach (25% within 90 days, 15% within 4–6 months) is workable. Two edits: (a) define "remaining committed spend" to exclude volume discounts applied after go-live; (b) require that the credit is paid as a one-time settlement within 30 days of termination notice.

2) Ramp language: change "return-to-commit clause" to explicitly call out measurement windows (30-day rolling average across months 3–4) and a remediation plan if usage remains below thresholds. This protects us from immediate churn gaming.

3) Audit & security: Bison must grant Redwood reasonable access to logs necessary to calculate actual usage; add a confidentiality carve-out for audit data. Also recommend not accepting any unlimited audit right in the MOU — scope it to usage reconciliation only.

4) Limitation: propose adding a cap to the customer's recourse tied to the early-exit credit (no further damages).

If we agree on these edits, I can prepare a redline for signature. Two asks before I finalize: confirm the $150k cap is acceptable to Finance, and Vivek's quick approval for the stepped credit so we can move fast.

-karthik
